# OS — the AGENTIK {OS} suite

This directory holds the AgentikOS product line: **73 operative systems**
in **9 groups**. Each subdirectory is ONE operative system.

The suite is surfaced in the TUI under the **OS** tab (`omega menu`) and
installed to `~/.omega/os/` by `install.sh`.

> An Agentik OS is not a prompt and not a document. It is a system with its
> own operating specification, workflows, commands, memory rules,
> evaluations and per-environment adapters, installed and run by the
> Agentik Runtime.

## Do not edit this file

`README.md`, the TUI roster (`crates/omega-core/src/os_products.rs`) and
`_registry.json` are all GENERATED from one source:

```
OS/_tools/suite.py          the registry: add or reorder an OS HERE
        |
        +-- suite.py registry        ->  OS/_registry.json
        +-- gen_os_products.py       ->  crates/omega-core/src/os_products.rs
        +-- gen_readme.py            ->  OS/README.md
        +-- scaffold.py build        ->  OS/<slug>/ file contract
```

After changing `suite.py`, re-run all four, then `cargo test -p omega-core`.

## The file contract

Every OS carries the same structure, so a user who learns one has learned
all of them and the Runtime can operate on any of them:

```
<slug>/
├── README.md      human entry point
├── OS.md          complete operating specification
├── SYSTEM.md      AI and system instructions
├── SKILL.md       capabilities and procedures
├── SETUP.md       initial configuration
├── manifest.json  machine-readable metadata
├── CHANGELOG.md   what changed between versions
├── WORKFLOWS/     repeatable processes
├── COMMANDS/      every command, explained
├── PROMPTS/       reusable prompt units
├── REFERENCES/    knowledge this OS needs
├── MEMORY/        what may be remembered, updated, forgotten
├── TOOLS/         external capabilities it may use
├── EVALS/         tests that prove it behaves correctly
├── EXAMPLES/      worked examples
├── INTERFACES/    chat, artifact, dashboard, generative UI
└── ADAPTERS/      chatgpt, claude, gemini, codex
```

## Reading the status column

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **authored** | Content written for this OS, beyond the scaffold |
| **scaffold** | Structure complete, content not yet authored |
| **absent** | Directory missing (a registry entry with no folder yet) |

Status is measured from disk at generation time, never asserted by hand.
